title: Case: A multi-parcel order arrives with one parcel still outstanding
context: An order consists of three separately tracked parcels. Two are received; the third must be traced by its own identifier.
initial_request: I received two of the three cartons for TG-7902. The missing carton is DL-4118-C. Please locate it; I am available tomorrow.

events.body: Order TG-7902 has parcels DL-4118-A, DL-4118-B and DL-4118-C. A and B have delivery scans; C has an inbound depot scan only. All three are required to complete the order.

I received two of the three cartons for TG-7902. The missing carton is DL-4118-C. Please locate it; I am available tomorrow.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-743.txt

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Nettlebank Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier to locate the missing parcel using its individual tracking ID.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Nettlebank Arc Logistics that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier to locate the missing parcel using its individual tracking ID. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: Closure is for the three-parcel count, not product quality or installation.
Treats label-scan-743.txt as evidence about DL-4118: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-67307)
Tells anyone that DL-4118 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-743.txt
expected.reference_message: Please trace DL-4118-C specifically and arrange its remaining delivery. Do not mark TG-7902 complete using only the A and B scans.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-020: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. label-scan-743.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-67307); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
